text: {"observations":"The clip is silent until about 6 s, then a steady, low-frequency-dominated sound begins and holds to the end (most energy below 1 kHz, centroid about 515 Hz). Peaks form a harmonic series near 75, 150, 225 and 300 Hz, and the ~155 Hz component glides smoothly down to ~144 Hz between 6 and 9.2 s. That slow continuous downward drift of a low harmonic drone suggests an engine changing speed or passing, which supports traffic noise (A). It argues against music (D), which would show stable discrete pitches and a clear rhythm; f0 salience is very low (~4-5%). There are no strong high-frequency tonal chirps above 2 kHz (the 1.5-8 kHz track is weak and erratic), which rules out bird chirping (B). The level is steady rather than showing loud broadband impacts, which makes construction noise (C) unlikely.","answer":"A"}
